interventions.step: Browser verification of the production build
interventions.action: Drove `next start` with a playwright-core copy already in the local npm cache (~/.npm/_npx) and the installed Google Chrome. The script lived in ./.scratch/verify. It checked layout at 390 and 1280 px, horizontal overflow, selection, the empty-name error, adding new and existing items, opening the Select from the keyboard with Escape and focus return, computed --ult-* values and color-scheme in explicit dark, explicit light and system mode, the portalled popup's theme, reduced motion, and the order of the production stylesheet.
interventions.reason: The guidance asks for a check of the production build in a browser in every mode, but it names no tool or command for that check, and init reports that it runs no browser checks.

interventions.action: Killed the `next start` process I had started earlier, which still held port 3107 and served stale chunks (resource 500s), then restarted the server on the new build.
interventions.reason: This was operational cleanup of my own test server. No guidance covers it.

decisions.choice: Category is chosen with an inline, portalled Ultima Select (Select.Portal to document.body) in a 'Log a donation' card, not a form in a Dialog
options: Portalled Select in an inline form
decisions.why: The brief allows either. An inline form keeps intake one step at the desk and on the phone. The root CSS theme reaches body portals, so no portal container is needed.

decisions.choice: The theme's Figtree / IBM Plex Mono faces are not loaded; the screen renders with the exported fallback stack (ui-sans-serif, system-ui, ...)
decisions.why: The export loads no font files and the guidance allows accepting the fallback. Loading Google Fonts would use a host other than the permitted public host, and there were no font files to self-host.

decisions.choice: Layout lengths and grid templates (content max width 72rem, 'minmax(0, 1fr)' and the 2fr/3fr split) are namespaced defineVars in an app token module, components/pantry/pantry.stylex.ts, not literals in stylex.create
options: App token module for every non-zero length and template
Literal values in the component's stylex.create, as the Projects lesson writes '100dvh' and grid templates
decisions.why: The brief forbids lengths decided outside theme and token modules. The Product semantic tokens lesson shows an application-owned defineVars module for app-only sizes.

decisions.choice: One breakpoint, const SPLIT = '@media (min-width: 48rem)', in pantry.tsx. Below it everything stacks in one column; above it the list sits beside the detail and the form
options: A larger laptop-only breakpoint such as 64rem
decisions.why: The guidance fixes where a breakpoint lives (a named module constant) but not its value. 48rem keeps a tablet or laptop-width window side by side while phones stack.

decisions.choice: Ran the optional Agent setup: `git init` in ./larder, then `ultima install --harness claude`, which wrote .claude/skills/ultima-design/SKILL.md and a PostToolUse hook in .claude/settings.json
options: Install for another harness (codex, cursor, copilot)
decisions.why: The init report marked this step optional and printed these commands. Installing it gives the project the installed skill that the brief lists as allowed guidance.

review.reviewer: Claude on mbp1, #774: transcript, request log, notes and production report
review.rule: An intervention is an action on the project or tooling that the guidance or CLI output did not print or link. A decision is an unresolved Ultima setup, theme or styling choice that changed the output. Product choices and documented alternatives do not count. Browser checks of the consumer application follow the guidance; rendering documentation to retrieve guidance or source would count.

decisions.choice: Put the screen's grid track templates (`minmax(0, 1fr)` and `minmax(0, 2fr) minmax(0, 3fr)`) in the app token module as `--app-columns-*` defineVars (components/pantry/pantry.stylex.ts) rather than as literals in stylex.create.
options: Literal track templates in the screen's stylex.create, as the Projects and list-detail lessons write them
defineVars in the application's own token module
decisions.why: The brief says the application decides no lengths outside its theme and token modules, with a breakpoint as the only exception. The lessons write grid templates literally. Neither says whether a track template is a length, and the Vite run on the same commit kept the literals (#845).

review.notes: The agent fetched llms.txt, the install, build-a-screen and support guides, and the list-detail, interaction-states, projects and product-tokens lessons over HTTP. It did not render documentation, decode a data link, extract a bundle, read CRM 01's registry source or reference the live host or another checkout. It ran init through --plan and --apply with no failed step (#835 not exercised). It installed the theme and components with shadcn@4.21.4, matching init and the printed commands (#836 holds). It imported ../ultima-theme.css after ./ultima.css in app/layout.tsx as install step 4 prints, set up ESLint as install#stylex-lint prints, and ran init's printed optional agent setup. The breakpoint is a named constant in pantry.tsx (#837 holds). Deleting init's setup-check preview follows the starter comment. Self-reported interventions are not counted. The browser check follows the printed hand step. The agent used a playwright-core copy it found in the machine's ~/.npm/_npx cache instead of installing one; that is equivalent to the installs earlier reviews did not count, but it shows the harness's per-run npm cache does not hide the user's npx cache (harness isolation, not guidance). Restarting its own stale `next start` server is test housekeeping, not an action on the project or Ultima tooling. The inspection of .next CSS carries out the printed cascade step. The self-reported decisions about Select vs Dialog, the font fallback, 48rem and agent setup are product choices or documented options. The grid-template placement is counted above. check, doctor, StyleX lint (0 errors), the raw-paint scan and all four external production cases passed. No operator edited the app.
